title: Quasi-likelihood
dek: Keep a mean μ(β) and a variance V(μ), drop a full density. The score still looks like a GLM score. The LRT is no longer χ² for free.
story: Wedderburn’s quasi-likelihood uses only E[Y] = μ(β) and Var(Y) = φ V(μ). The quasi-score is ∑ (∂μ/∂β) (y − μ) / (φ V(μ)), the same shape as an exponential-family score. IRLS still runs. You get β̂ and a dispersion φ̂, usually Pearson χ² / df.
Quasi-Poisson: V(μ) = μ, φ > 1 inflates SEs by √φ relative to Poisson. Quasi-binomial: V = μ(1−μ), φ > 1 for extra-binomial variation. These are not models for P(Y=y); they are estimating equations.

Because there is no fully specified ℓ, a “likelihood ratio” is a difference in quasi-deviance. Its reference is not automatically χ². Sandwich Wald or an F-style adjustment with φ̂ is the matching language. Do not print a Poisson LRT next to a quasi-Poisson fit and call it one analysis.
deepTitle: What you lose when you drop the density
deep: Consistency of β̂ still wants a correct mean. φ and V handle second moments. If the mean is wrong, quasi-likelihood is consistently wrong with honest-ish SEs.

AIC/BIC need a likelihood. Quasi-AIC variants exist as heuristics; they are not the AIC theorem. For genuine model comparison of mean structures, a nested quasi-deviance test with an F reference (φ estimated) is the usual compromise.

Negative binomial is a real likelihood with a second parameter k for overdispersion. It is not the same as quasi-Poisson: weights and predictions differ, and NB can be compared with LRTs. Use NB if you need a pmf (predictive intervals, AIC).
GEE is quasi-likelihood with a working correlation across clusters. The sandwich is mandatory. It estimates population-average β, not the cluster-conditional β of a mixed GLM.

example.title: Quasi-Poisson on weekly cases
example.setup: n = 52 weeks, Poisson GLM residual Pearson χ² = 140 on 50 df. Covariate: rain. Model-based se(β_rain) = 0.08.

steps.title: Point estimate
steps.body: β̂_rain is the same as Poisson IRLS with V = μ. Only the SE and tests change if you keep the same mean.

steps.title: If you need a likelihood
steps.body: Fit NB(μ, k), quote AIC or an LRT for rain inside NB. That is a different second-moment model, not a relabeling of φ̂.

example.takeaway: Quasi multiplies SEs when V is the right shape and φ is not 1. It does not create a density.

choices: A mean map and a variance function (plus a scale), not necessarily a density
check.answer: A mean map and a variance function (plus a scale), not necessarily a density
check.why: That is the point of “quasi.” AIC and LRTs lose their free χ² licence.

whyWrong.A full pmf/pdf for Y: That would be a GLM family.

check.prompt: Poisson se = 0.10, φ̂ = 4. Quasi-Poisson se is:
On the nested plate, why is AIC listed in the outer (density) box?
check.figureHint: Full box includes true ℓ and AIC/LRT.
choices: Because AIC is a sandwich estimator
Because AIC is defined from a likelihood; quasi-deviance is not that object
Because quasi-likelihood maximises AIC by construction
Because φ̂ is the AIC penalty
check.answer: Because AIC is defined from a likelihood; quasi-deviance is not that object
check.why: The plate is a licence map. Inner box: estimating equations. Outer box: genuine ℓ.

whyWrong.Because φ̂ is the AIC penalty: AIC penalty is parameter count (or effective df).
